subject.statement: Bob Iger is currently the CEO of Disney.

summary: Verdict: FALSE – Bob Iger is not the CEO of Disney as of 2026-10-01. He stepped down as CEO on 2026-03-18, became Senior Advisor and board member, and Josh D'Amaro succeeded him as CEO.

findings.statement: Bob Iger stepped down as CEO effective March 18, 2026 and transitioned to a Senior Advisor role.
As of October 1, 2026, Disney's official leadership page lists Bob Iger as Senior Advisor and board member, not as CEO.
SEC filings from May and August 2026 still listed Robert A. Iger as Chief Executive Officer at the time of filing, showing a reporting lag after his March departure.

conflicts: As of 2026-10-01, what is Bob Iger's official title at The Walt Disney Company according to Disney's latest SEC filing, press release, or corporate website? - supported by equilar.com, fortune.com, latimes.com, variety.com, wikidata.org (weight 2.85) vs refuted by cnbc.com, content.edgar-online.com, d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net, en.wikipedia.org, nypost.com, sec.gov, stocktitan.net (weight 4.15)
What does Disney's latest SEC filing or press release (as of 2026-10-01) state as Bob Iger's official title? - supported by sec.gov (weight 0.57) vs refuted by cnbc.com (weight 0.85)
conflict_notes: Conflict over Q3 (official title per latest SEC filing, press release, or corporate website): supporting sources (equilar.com, fortune.com, latimes.com, variety.com, wikidata.org) total weight 2.85 vs refuting sources (cnbc.com, content.edgar-online.com, d18rn0p25nwr6d.cloudfront.net, en.wikipedia.org, nypost.com, sec.gov, stocktitan.net) total weight 4.15. The refuting sources were given greater weight because they include direct, dated announcements of the successor (e.g., latimes.com, nypost.com, sec.gov filings naming Josh D'Amaro as CEO effective March 18, 2026) and multiple independent news outlets, outweighing the indirect support from wikidata and equivocal filings.

Conflict over Q4 (what Disney's latest SEC filing or press release states as title): supporting source sec.gov (weight 0.57) vs refuting cnbc.com (weight 0.85). The refuting source received more weight because it provides a clear, dated announcement of the successor effective March 18, 2026, while the supporting SEC filing only reflects data up to August 2026 and does not address the title after the transition.
